THE BENCHMARK RAN, FOR REAL. ES-17 made a matrix cell able to reach a provider, so it was run at protocol strength: k=5, arms off/on, each cell a spawned child over a freshly seeded fixture home, from TWO independently seeded isolated homes, against local Ollama serving gemma4:12b. Run A measured_tasks 3/3 with absent_cells 2; Run B 3/3 with absent_cells 0; both name LocalOllama:gemma4:12b in provider_binding and in the pin, with spend observed on every contributing cell. The 2026-09-06 attempt got measured_tasks 0 and 100/100 VERIFIER_ABSENT. V4 IS UNMET, AND THIS TIME THE REFUSAL IS A RESULT RATHER THAN A RAIL — that distinction is the whole finding. Four of five stated-variance conditions hold across two separately built homes (same task_set_version, same scenario_sha256 set, same prompt_pack_sha256, same config_snapshot_ref). 'Same verdict class per task' is FALSE, with 2 of 3 tasks flipping. On 2026-09-06 that condition was false because both classes were null — the rail that stops a benchmark which never ran from certifying itself. It is now false because two REAL classes moved. The setup reproduces; the verdict does not. Filed as #2587. REAL-PROVIDER USE ASSERTED ON THE INNER MODEL AXIS, because the outer factory returns a wrapper and isinstance(x, ScriptedProvider) is False passes vacuously — ES-17 hit exactly that. The chain was walked in a cell-shaped throwaway home down to OpenAIProvider with _base_url http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1 and _model gemma4:12b. TENTH INSTANCE OF THE ABSENT-VS-DECLARED-FALSE CLASS, and the first at SCHEMA-VERSION level: the results page now renders THREE provenance states and the third is the trap — an object means cells called a real model; null means the run RECORDED that nothing was bound; the key being ABSENT means provenance is UNRECORDED, because ES-17 added the field without moving REPORT_SCHEMA (#2562). 'We never recorded it' is not 'we recorded that no model ran', so the panel branches on KEY PRESENCE rather than truthiness. AND THE PIN IS NOT PROVENANCE, which it previously read as: compute_pin takes model_fingerprint from the INVOKING HOME's active_models.json, so it names what the operator configured whether or not any of it crossed the cell boundary — measured, a bound run and an unbound run from the SAME bound home carry an identical pin.model_fp (5970c589da34) while the unbound one reached no provider at all (#2561). THE PUBLISHED RESULT WAS GIVING ADVICE ABOUT A DIFFERENT EXPERIMENT: harness/learning_verdict.py forwarded compare()'s notes untouched, breaking its own docstring promise in the same file, so a skills artifact told the reader to 'give the cheaper arm more budget... the largest published fan-out win was ~3.75x tokens' — a lever this experiment does not have. Now replaced in skills-arm words from the numbers compare() already computed, detected BY VOCABULARY rather than by matching upstream prose, so a reworded upstream note cannot slip through. The inconclusive-band note is deliberately NOT reworded: its parenthetical is the literature citation justifying the 5-point band, and 'rewording a citation to suit another experiment misquotes it'. Unequal arms now say so — sk_task_project lost two cells to VERIFIER_ABSENT and was verdicted on 3 trials against 5, so its 0.5139 ratio read as a 48.6% spend difference that is mostly two missing trials (per-trial 0.857); deliberately NOT normalised, because that number is fanout_measure's to produce. Also fixed: §8 promises the verdict is published with its notes, spread AND token ratio, but notes and ratio were dropped — so a not_token_matched row, 4 of the 6 rows a real run produces, was the verdict alone. FOUR FALSIFICATIONS, each red-then-green with the mutation restored in the same invocation. One caught a real drift: deriving the percentage from the payload's 4-decimal token_ratio printed 13.7% where compare() printed 13.6%, so it is asserted against compare()'s own printed note rather than a literal. REMAINING = CLAUSE 3 ONLY, and both halves are owner-side. (a) THE SITE HALF IS STRUCTURALLY BLOCKED: personalclaw.dev pins core at v0.1.3/bc185c02 and sync-docs.mjs's TREES are guides/reference/architecture/security/research, with its own comment 'Deliberately NOT synced: docs/roadmap/ (intent, not released behavior — the projection rule)'. The methodology doc lives in that excluded tree, so the shipped path CANNOT carry this page. It needs an owner decision on which synced tree a results page belongs in, then a release tag, a sources-pin bump and a deploy. (b) THE HONEST README ONE-LINER (T4.3) is still unwritten and THE REASON HAS CHANGED: it is no longer 'there is nothing to be honest about'. The one honest sentence available today is 'we ran it and it does not reproduce', and a README announcing a benchmark whose verdict flips between runs is the same overclaim in the other direction. Write it when #2587 resolves. CEILING, stated rather than papered over: register coverage is WALL-CLOCK, not capability — these runs cover 3 of 10 register tasks, and the full register at k=5 is ~5h per run on this hardware (~155s per cell; run_matrix is sequential by design and the local Ollama runs -np 1), so a two-run V4 check over the whole register is a ~10h job. task_set_fingerprint() reports all ten tasks regardless of --task, so the pin and task-set conditions are unaffected. |
